title: HbA1c blood test
what: A blood test that shows your average blood sugar over the last 2 to 3 months. One short spike in sugar barely affects it.
why: To find diabetes or prediabetes, and to check how treatment is working if you already have diabetes.
duration: usually 5 minutes; blood is taken from a vein
tell_doctor: If you have anemia or recently lost a lot of blood
If you had a blood transfusion in recent months

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually you do not need an empty stomach. You can have the test at any time. If you also have a blood sugar test, come in the morning before eating.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Take your medicines as usual. If you are not sure, tell your doctor. They will decide.

bring: Your referral, if you have one
Past results of this test, to compare
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tied above your elbow
The skin is wiped, and blood is taken from a vein into a tube
A cotton ball is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a mosquito bite
Sometimes a small bruise is left afterwards
after: You can eat and go back to your usual day right away
Your doctor explains the result and compares it with normal levels and your past tests

faq.q: Do I need an empty stomach for an HbA1c test?
faq.a: Usually not. It shows your sugar over 2 to 3 months, so breakfast barely affects the result.

faq.q: How often should I have this test if I have diabetes?
faq.a: Usually every 3 months if your treatment is being changed. When your sugar is stable, less often. Your doctor will give you the exact schedule.
